# `scripts/fp/traffic/`

## `scripts/fp/traffic/ambient.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Ambient filler (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §6): unnamed commuters (some of them cyclists) and pedestrians around the player, denser where sim.traffic and residents' trip_load are high (caps 40 vehicles, 60 people). The caps are spent where they can be seen: cars live within CAR_RING (just past VIS_CAR) and people within PED_RING (just past VIS_PERSON), both inside TRAFFIC_RADIUS. Cars appear and vanish only beyond MIN_SPAWN and out of the camera's view; people appear out of view beyond PED_MIN_SPAWN, or fade in (render.gd) far enough away that the fade is all one sees. A synchronous fill (first fill, load, teleport: the whole view is new) places agents anywhere outside the player's personal space. Also the curb parking that makes streets look lived in: deterministic per slot, so it never changes as the player walks.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/body_spheres.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The posed body's collision points, and the press-out that keeps a knocked-down or thrown body out of the geometry its clips sweep it into. of() gives [feet, torso, head] from the drawn feet and the head (people.gd head_of -- the posed bone while a body draws it, else the standing estimate); a clip that lies the body down puts the head and torso far past whatever stopped the feet, so reactions.gd measures all three. press_out() eases the whole drawn body along the shallowest way clear whenever a reaction runs.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `OBB = preload("res://scripts/fp/obb2d.gd")`
- `BODY_R = 0.25 * WS.M`
- `HEAD_R = 0.14 * WS.M`

### Functions

- `static func of(feet: Vector3, head: Vector3) -> Array[Vector3]`: The collision points of the body drawn from feet: [feet, torso, head], the torso between them (the last is the head -- whatever rad_of says of it).
- `static func rad_of(k: int) -> float`: Radius of the k-th sphere of of() (the head and anything past it).
- `static func press_out(w: WK.Walker, extent: Callable, collision: CollisionWorld, cars: Array = []) -> void`: Eases the whole drawn body out of whatever the clips have pressed it into, along the shallowest way clear, while a reaction runs. Horizontal only -- the flight keeps its arc. However deep, this tick: the sweeps that put the body past its feet (a fall, a get-up fold, a flight's tilt) move it faster than any lean could ease, and a capped ease would trail 30 cm into a wall by the fold's end. A full correction reads as the body sliding along what stopped it; the shallow presses stay as subtle as before. cars holds the moving car bodies the static world does not (traffic's near cars as [xz centre, yaw, Vector2(half width, half length), y bottom, y top]): a body thrown or slid into a real car comes clear of it the same way, or it would lie inside the drawn vehicle with nothing to press it out.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/car_doors.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The driver's door of a full car model (vehicles_v2) as a part of its own that swings open on a hinge at its front edge. The generator (tools/blender/realcity/vehicles2.py) builds each body as one mesh and draws the doors' shut lines down its sides as thin dark strips from just above the sill to under the belt; the driver's door lies between the strips around the driver's seat (Seat_Driver, on +X; the models face +Z). The cut takes, between those lines and above the strips' foot: the outer skin and what sits on it (handle, trim, the mirror), the door card behind it, and above the belt the side glass with its frame. Triangles that cross a shut line or the foot are split there, so the shut door shows no seam. Once per model (cached); a drawn car gets its door on demand (pose) and keeps it, shut, when its node goes back to the pool. Lengths below are model units (the generator's metre is WS.M).

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `SEAT_NODE = "Seat_Driver"`
- `OPEN_ANGLE = deg_to_rad(68.0)`: Fully open, the rear edge has swung out by this angle (radians).
- `STRIP_W = 0.03 * WS.M`: A shut-line strip: at most STRIP_W along the car, at least STRIP_SPAN of the body height tall, STRIP_TRIS triangles or more, facing out (+X) beyond STRIP_SIDE of the half width.
- `STRIP_JOIN = 0.015 * WS.M`
- `STRIP_SPAN = 0.35`
- `STRIP_TRIS = 6`
- `STRIP_SIDE = 0.6`
- `STRIP_OFF = 0.0012 * WS.M`: The strips stand this far off the skin (side_line's out) and stop this far under the belt.
- `BELT_ABOVE = 0.015 * WS.M`
- `DOOR_MIN = 0.7 * WS.M`: A door is DOOR_MIN to DOOR_MAX long; vans draw no line behind the front door, which then ends DOOR_FALLBACK behind its front line.
- `DOOR_MAX = 1.7 * WS.M`
- `DOOR_FALLBACK = 0.95 * WS.M`
- `SKIN_IN = 0.024 * WS.M`: Below the belt the door is the skin and what is on it (within SKIN_IN inside it) and the door card (facing in, within CARD_IN); above it the side glass and its frame (facing out, within GLASS_IN of the line from the belt to the glass top) and what stands out past the belt line (the mirror, within MIRROR_IN).
- `CARD_IN = 0.12 * WS.M`
- `GLASS_IN = 0.03 * WS.M`
- `MIRROR_IN = 0.012 * WS.M`
- `GLASS_NX = 0.85`
- `CARD_NX = -0.7`
- `GLASS_MIN = 0.2 * WS.M`: The side glass reaches at least this far over the belt (a truck's cab corner has none).
- `HANDLE_BACK = 0.24 * WS.M`: The handle sits this far ahead of the door's rear edge and under the belt (vehicles2 handle).
- `HANDLE_DOWN = 0.075 * WS.M`
- `ON_PLANE = 1e-7`: Points this close to a cutting plane count as on it.

### Inner classes

- `Door`: One model's driver's door. Points and planes are in the body mesh's space.
- `Cut`: Vertex arrays being cut: the source's attributes plus the points made on the cutting planes.

### Functions

- `static func of(key: String, scene: PackedScene) -> Door`: The door of the model `scene` (cached under key); check .ok.
- `static func pose(node: Node3D, d: Door, amount: float) -> bool`: Shows node's door opened by amount (0 shut .. 1 open), cutting it out of the body the first time it opens. Returns false when the model has no door.
- `static func points(d: Door) -> Dictionary`: The door's key points in the model's own space (its root node's): the hinge, the handle, the driver's seat (hip point), the rear edge at the belt and that edge with the door wide open.
- `static func skin_x(d: Door, y: float, z: float) -> float`: The outer skin's x at height y (below the belt) at z, from the two lines' profiles.
- `static func is_door(d: Door, c: Vector3, n: Vector3) -> bool`: True when a piece of surface centred at c, facing n, belongs to the door (inside its lines).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/carjack.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Taking a car with someone at the wheel (the carjack flag; docs/fp/ARCHITECTURE.md, Driving): a car stopped or crawling in traffic is the player's to take, an ambient driver's or a resident's, and its driver is dragged out first. They come out beside the driver's door and are knocked down away from the car by a blow of cause "carjack" (traffic_feature.gd hit_walker: reactions.gd has them lie a moment, get up, shout and run off; incidents.gd has them and those who saw it remember it, and calls the police). Drawn at the wheel, they are dragged out of the seat over the sill first (reactions.gd drag_out) and the blow throws them JACK_FLING clear of the door. They run for the sidewalk round the car's rear, not through it. A resident's trip goes on on foot from there (trips.gd on_carjacked); an ambient driver wanders on along the sidewalk. Either keeps the look they had at the wheel (occupants.gd).

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `SW = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/sidewalks.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `TRIPS = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/trips.gd")`
- `OUT = 0.3 * WS.M`: The driver comes out OUT beyond the body side, level with the seat, and takes a blow of STRENGTH (hard enough to knock them down, reactions.gd DOWN) straight out from the car. Their way off the road passes CLEAR out from the car's rear corner on that side.
- `STRENGTH = 0.85`
- `CLEAR = 1.2 * WS.M`
- `JACK_FLING = 1.8`

### Properties

- `f: Object`: the traffic feature

### Functions

- `func setup(p_f: Object) -> void`
- `static func occupied(c: VH.Car) -> bool`: True when c is a car on the road with someone at the wheel: an ambient driver or a resident.
- `func eject(c: VH.Car, src: Vector3) -> Dictionary`: Drags car c's driver out, the hero standing at src: they come out beside the driver's door, knocked down away from the car, and set off on foot once they are up. c is left for the caller to take (its trip let go). Returns the person_hit info, {} when nobody could be put there.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/contact_shadows.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Contact shadows: a soft dark patch on the ground under every drawn vehicle and person, all in one MultiMesh draw. The sun's shadow maps reach only some of them (full and mid-LOD vehicles to render.SHADOW_DIST, people bodies to people.T1_NEAR, nothing after dark or under cloud), and without darkening where a body meets the road, a parked car or a walker seems to hover.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/crowd_reacts.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The crowd's answer to what the street sees and hears, split out of reactions.gd (which keeps the Reaction records, the blow, the fall and the witness loop that picks who reacts): a knock-down rocks the onlookers who stay back as one (crowd_gasp), and the hero's horn startles the people it reaches (horn_street). Wired like fight_back.gd: the walkers, the roll and the record lifecycle shared from reactions.gd's setup, the records untyped, and reactions.gd's clock read through now.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `GASP_TIP = 0.12`: A knock-down the street sees (severity 2) rocks the onlookers who stay back as one (crowd_gasp): no beat of looking first, a sharp backward tip (GASP_TIP rad over GASP_S) before they shout. Once per crowd: another body falling within GASP_CD seconds and GASP_R of the last gets the plain reaction.
- `GASP_S = 0.5`
- `GASP_CD = 6.0`
- `GASP_R = 10.0 * WS.M`
- `HORN_TIP = 0.08`: A horn (horn_street) startles the people it reaches: a beat turned toward the car, rocked back a touch (HORN_TIP over HORN_TIP_S), the ones within HORN_NEAR stepping back off the road — a long press reaches HORN_LONG_NEAR and they shake their head at it. Once per crowd: a horn within HORN_CD seconds and HORN_R of the last gets no answer. One exception: a long press on the heels of its own tap (within ESCALATE_S, from the same place within ESCALATE_R) escalates the ripple in flight instead — the cooldown is for honk spam, not for leaning on the horn.
- `HORN_TIP_S = 0.4`
- `HORN_NEAR = 8.0 * WS.M`
- `HORN_LONG_NEAR = 12.0 * WS.M`
- `HORN_STEP = 0.25 * WS.M`
- `HORN_CD = 5.0`
- `HORN_R = 20.0 * WS.M`
- `ESCALATE_S = 1.0`
- `ESCALATE_R = 2.0 * WS.M`
- `RING_MIN = 3`: A brawl with a ring on it (brawl_ring — three or more fighting the hero) draws jeers from the crowd: every JEER_CD seconds one of the onlookers within JEER_R of the hero turns to the fight and shouts a beat (JEER_S). The fight's own never jeer (they are not free). Which onlooker answers picks off the same seeded hash as the fight rolls (fight_seeded_rolls), never the shared stream, so unrelated reactions running first change nothing for it.
- `JEER_CD = 1.4`
- `JEER_R = 10.0 * WS.M`
- `JEER_S = 0.9`

### Properties

- `wk: WK`: Shared from reactions.gd's setup: the walkers, the roll, the record lifecycle and the clock.
- `base_seed: int`: The sim seed reactions.gd's setup() hands over beside the shared stream: the seeded jeer pick (fight_seeded_rolls) keys on it, so a fresh fixture without setup() (base_seed 0) is deterministic too.
- `active: Dictionary`: The live reactions (walker id -> record), for the horn escalation to find the tap's own.

### Functions

- `func seed_setup(seed: int) -> void`: reactions.gd's setup() hands the sim seed over beside the shared stream; the seeded jeer pick's counter restarts with each setup, so a re-seeded fixture replays the same jeers.
- `func gasp_due(at: Vector3) -> bool`: True when a knock-down at at may rock the crowd as one (crowd_gasp): the flag on, and no gasp within GASP_CD seconds and GASP_R of it.
- `func apply_gasp(r) -> void`: r is one of the crowd who stays: it rocks back as one with them — no beat of looking first, a sharp backward tip before the shout.
- `func noted_gasp(at: Vector3) -> void`: The gasp played: the crowd round at is quiet for GASP_CD seconds.
- `func step(dt: float) -> void`: The crowd's beat (reactions.gd's step): while a brawl has a ring on it (brawl_ring), someone near turns to the fight and jeers, one per JEER_CD seconds.
- `func startle(src: Vector3, radius: float, long: bool) -> Array`: A car horn sounded at src and carries radius (u; horn_street): the people it reaches who are free startle — a beat turned toward the car, rocked back a touch, the ones within HORN_NEAR stepping back off the road and then composing themselves (a long press reaches HORN_LONG_NEAR and they shake their head at it). Honk spam gets no answer: one ripple per HORN_CD seconds within HORN_R of the last. Returns those startled.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/fight_back.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The scrap and the care for a body on the ground: fighting back, the tempers, counter cues and downed awareness, split out of reactions.gd. reactions.gd keeps the Reaction records, the blow, the fall and the street watching; this layer borrows the records through the state setup() shares (the active table by reference, the _new/_free/_after callables) and stays untyped about Reaction so the two classes never preload each other. reactions.gd drives it: begin() from _next_step, step_fight()/step_check() from the step match, the rest from hit(), witness() and _after().

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `FIGHT_ODDS = {"shove": 0.3, "punch": 0.4}`: Fighting back (fight_back): the share of those shoved or punched (and not knocked down) who do, by cause (fight_odds starts as this); how long a fight may last (s); how close they come (feet to feet; within FIGHT_SLACK of it counts), from how far they run there and beyond how far they give up.
- `FIGHT_S = 20.0`
- `FIGHT_REACH = 0.9 * WS.M`
- `FIGHT_SLACK = 0.05 * WS.M`
- `FIGHT_RUN = 3.0 * WS.M`
- `FIGHT_LOST = 12.0 * WS.M`
- `FIGHT_BLOWS = [[&"punch_jab", 0.2, 0.45, 0.7], [&"punch_cross", 0.29, 0.6, 0.8]]`: Their punches in turn: [clip, contact time (s), strength 0..1, seconds the clip plays]; the pause between two (s) and before the first.
- `FIGHT_GAP = Vector2(0.45, 1.1)`
- `FIGHT_FIRST = 0.25`
- `WIND_RATE = 0.5`: A punch at the hero holds its clip back at WIND_RATE through the first half of the run to contact, then plays at 2 - WIND_RATE, so the clip arrives with the blow's own timing (counter_cues): the wind-up reads, the strike snaps, the counter window never moves.
- `FIGHT_HIT = 1.25 * WS.M`: A punch lands on the hero within FIGHT_HIT (feet to feet) inside the cone ahead (the cosine), from the fist FIST ahead and up (metres), and pushes them on at FIGHT_PUSH (u/s).
- `FIGHT_CONE = 0.5`
- `FIST = Vector2(0.5, 1.45)`
- `FIGHT_PUSH = 1.5 * WS.M`
- `TEMPERS = ["plain", "guard", "dancer", "caller", "bolt", "bruiser"]`: How a fighter fights (fight_tempers), in pick order with their shares: a temper is fixed to who the fighter is — their walker id and resident id hashed into the shares, so the same person always fights the same way whatever the order of things around them. One plain; a guard turns GUARD_SHARE of the hero's blows that reach them while the scrap is theirs; a dancer sidesteps their way (by id parity) round the ring at DANCE_W (rad/s); a caller brings at most CALL_MAX of those near enough to see in with them; a bolt's scrap lasts BOLT_S before they run; a bruiser leads with the cross and answers a blow the moment it lands.
- `TEMPER_SHARE = [0.34, 0.18, 0.16, 0.12, 0.1, 0.1]`
- `T_PLAIN = 0`
- `T_GUARD = 1`
- `T_DANCER = 2`
- `T_CALLER = 3`
- `T_BOLT = 4`
- `T_BRUISER = 5`
- `GUARD_SHARE = 0.45`
- `DANCE_W = 0.7`
- `CALL_MAX = 2`
- `BOLT_S = 2.5`
- `CHIP_HIT = 0.26`: A guard's guard wears out (guard_chip): every blow turned aside chips it by CHIP_HIT plus CHIP_K times the blow's strength, and the one that takes it past 1 lands in full instead. Beaten, the guard drops for BREAK_S (guard_break): the fighter stands off balance, throwing nothing and turning nothing aside, until the guard knits back whole and can be chipped anew.
- `CHIP_K = 0.2`
- `BREAK_S = 1.2`
- `DISARM_ODDS = 0.35`: The share of turned-aside blows that knock a swung weapon out of the hero's hand (weapon_disarm), so a guard costs you the bat now and then, not every other swing. Rolled on who they are and their count of turn-asides this scrap (temper_of's way: a hash, never the shared roll), so the same scrap always disarms on the same blow.
- `RING_SLOTS = 2`: The brawl ring (brawl_ring): more than RING_SLOTS fighting the hero slot by arrival (slot_seq, taken as the scrap starts) — the first two engage as ever, the rest hold the ring at RING_R, facing in and punching nothing, until a slot ahead opens (one down or out of the fight) and they step in. The crowd round them jeers (crowd_reacts.gd's step). Off: every fighter piles in at once.
- `RING_R = 2.2 * WS.M`
- `CHECK_R = 6.0 * WS.M`: Downed awareness (downed_awareness): a blow that leaves someone down brings the nearest free onlooker within CHECK_R over to look — they come within CHECK_NEAR (feet to feet), lean in (rad, + forward) with a slow head shake for CHECK_S, then walk on; once for each knock-down. A fighter whose hero goes down stands over them a beat (STAND_OVER_S) before walking off. CHECK_CAP bounds the walk over.
- `CHECK_NEAR = 0.8 * WS.M`
- `CHECK_S = 2.4`
- `CHECK_LEAN = 0.3`
- `CHECK_CAP = 9.0`
- `STAND_OVER_S = 1.3`
- `RUN_F = 2.6`: A walker's own speed times this is their run; the fighter capsule radii (u) handed to the collision world. Both as reactions.gd (its RUN_F, BODY_R and BODY_H).
- `BODY_R = 0.25 * WS.M`
- `BODY_H = 1.7 * WS.M`
- `WITNESS_R = 8.0 * WS.M`: How near a brawler's call for friends reaches, as reactions.gd's WITNESS_R.

### Properties

- `hero_open: bool`: The hero can be fought now (on foot and in control; traffic sets it every step), and who hears of a punch that lands on them: on_hero_hit(at, strength, push).
- `hero_down: bool`: The hero is down on the ground now (traffic sets it every step beside hero_open; downed_awareness).
- `on_wind_up: Callable`: Who hears of a punch thrown at the hero as it starts: on_wind_up(walker id, fist, seconds until it lands); and who may counter it as it lands: on_hero_parry(walker id, fist) -> true when it is countered (it then misses).
- `fight_odds: Dictionary`: The share who fight back, by cause (test hook), and the punches that landed on the hero or were countered.
- `fight_temper: Dictionary`: Walker id -> their temper among TEMPERS (a test hook, overriding the identity hash), and the share of the hero's blows a guard turns aside (a test hook too).
- `last_disarm`: Whether the blow just turned aside would knock a swung weapon loose (weapon_disarm): reactions.hit reads it into the res. And walker id -> their count of turn-asides this scrap (the disarm roll's seed; reset as the scrap starts).
- `base_seed: int`: The sim seed reactions.gd's setup() hands over with the shared stream: the seeded rolls (fight_seeded_rolls) key on it, so a fresh fixture without setup() (base_seed 0) is deterministic too.
- `active: Dictionary`: reactions.gd's live state, shared at setup: walker id -> Reaction of everyone down or reacting, the spawner of a Reaction for a walker (_new), the "may start a reaction" test (_free) and the after-blow planner (_after, for a turned-aside blow's scrap going on).

### Functions

- `func temper_of(w: WK.Walker) -> int`: w's temper among TEMPERS: the test pin (fight_temper) wins, else it is fixed to who w is (fight_tempers) — their id and resident id hashed into the shares, so the same person always fights the same way whatever the order of things around them. Plain without the flag.
- `func arm(r) -> void`: A fighter's temper, and their way round the hero, fixed; a fresh scrap starts with a whole guard (guard_chip).
- `func fights_back(r, cause: String) -> bool`: True when r's walker fights the hero back: always once they have, else by fight_odds for the cause while the hero can be fought. A fighter's temper is fixed the moment they square up.
- `func turned_aside(r, cause: String, strength: float) -> bool`: True when the hero's blow lands on a guarded fighter's guard instead (fight_tempers): the scrap is still theirs (fighting, or waiting to) and they turn guard_share of the blows that reach them aside. Nothing of it counts: no reel back, no slide, nothing toward the knock-down. But the guard wears (guard_chip): each blow turned aside chips it, and the one that takes the chip past 1 lands in full — the beaten guard dropping a beat (guard_break): off balance, everything landing, until it knits back.
- `func guarded_plan(r, cause: String) -> StringName`: The blow they turned aside (fight_tempers): a short duck behind the guard, then the scrap goes on as it was. Plans the steps; the caller (reactions.hit) starts them.
- `func after_fight(r) -> Array`: A fighter's plan once the blow is over (fight_tempers): a caller shouts their call longer and drafts friends into it; the scrap itself and what follows it are fight_steps.
- `func fight_steps(r) -> Array`: The scrap and what follows it, by temper (fight_tempers): a bolt's fight is short and ends in them running off; anyone else's may run its course and ends in a walk back.
- `func call_friends(r) -> void`: A caller drafts friends into the scrap (fight_tempers): up to CALL_MAX of the people around within WITNESS_R who are free shout with them, square up and join in, each their own way.
- `func run_step() -> Array`
- `func send_checker(r) -> void`: Sends the nearest free onlooker within CHECK_R to look r's downed victim over (downed_awareness): once for each knock-down, and never one of the fight's own. The checker walks up beside the body, leans in a moment, then walks on (the "check" step, step_check).
- `func step_check(r, dt: float) -> bool`: The checker walks up beside the body they came for, then leans over it with a slow head shake (CHECK_S) and walks on. Over at once when the one they came for is up again or gone. A hand's width past CHECK_NEAR counts as arrived: the walk clamps at the ring, and without the slack a landing exactly on it would never tip into the lean.
- `func begin(r) -> void`: The first step of a scrap (reactions' _next_step calls this as a "fight" step starts): blows come in pairs from FIGHT_FIRST on; a bruiser leads with the cross and answers a blow the moment it lands (fight_tempers).
- `func step_fight(r, dt: float) -> bool`: Fighting back: squares up to the hero, closes in to FIGHT_REACH and throws a punch whenever the pause is over. Over (true) once the punch under way is done and the hero cannot be fought, is FIGHT_LOST away or the step's time is up.
- `func dancing(r) -> bool`: A dancer sidesteps while they wait for their punch (fight_tempers).
- `func orbit(r, dist: float, dt: float) -> void`: A dancer steps their own way round the hero on the ring of FIGHT_REACH (fight_tempers), facing them all the while: near enough to punch from, never still for the hero to line up.
- `func close_in(r, dir: Vector3, room: float, dt: float) -> void`: Runs at the hero from afar and walks the last metres (by at most room), stopped by walls and posts.
- `func punch(r, dt: float, dist: float) -> void`: The punch under way: at its contact time it reaches a hero still within FIGHT_HIT in the cone ahead (reach_hero); once the clip has played, the next punch of the pair waits a pause.
- `func reach_hero(w: WK.Walker, strength: float) -> void`: w's punch of strength reaches the hero: countered (on_hero_parry), it misses; else it lands (on_hero_hit).
- `static func fist(w: WK.Walker) -> Vector3`: Where w's fist lands: FIST ahead of and up from its drawn feet.
- `func set_feet(w: WK.Walker, q: Vector3) -> void`: Draws w's feet at q, on the ground there (off the curb into the road, say).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/fleets.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

City fleets on lanes in first person (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §5): buses on 2-4 seeded closed lines through the bus stops (they pull in at each shelter, people board and alight), delivery and garbage trucks, and emergency crews that run to incidents with sirens (through red lights at walking pace once the box is clear), wait at the scene, and drive back to the station. CityLife asks for vehicles through spawn_fleet / dispatch_crew; drivers are residents with the matching job when one is free, else "city crew".

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `DWELL = 9.0`
- `MAX_CREWS = 10`
- `ASTAR_PER_FRAME = 4`: Crew routes are A* builds: at most this many per frame (the feature refills the budget), the rest wait in `pending` (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §1).
- `CURB_LAT = 0.055`
- `CALL_MAX = 240.0`: A crew answering a call (stay > 0) gives up after this long (s) from setting off.
- `JOBS = {"bus": "bus driver", "truck": "truck driver", "garbage_truck": "sanitation worker", "f...`

### Properties

- `stop_sides: Dictionary`: tile -> side index of its shelter
- `last_dispatch_fail: String`: Why the last crew build sent nobody ("" when it sent a crew); for tests and logs.
- `pending: Array`: Crew requests waiting for an A* slot: [kind, station, target, stay]; crews waiting to route home.
- `astar_left: int`: A* builds left this frame.
- `retry_t: float`: Seconds before stale lines may be rebuilt again, and the current wait (it doubles while the rebuild keeps failing: a failed A* is the expensive case).

### Inner classes

- `Line`: A closed bus line: stops (tiles) in order, the lane beside each shelter and the legs between.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_f: Object, p_sim: CitySim, p_lg: LG, p_vh: VH) -> void`
- `func read_stops(view: CityView) -> Dictionary`: Shelter side of every bus stop (G1 may store it as a Vector2i; else inferred like CityView).
- `func stops_signature(view: CityView) -> String`: Signature of the stop set (lines rebuild when it changes).
- `func rebuild_lines(view: CityView) -> int`: Rebuilds the seeded lines from the current stops. Returns the number of lines.
- `func stale() -> bool`: True when the lines no longer match the roads: none although two stops exist (the roads between them may have been missing when the stops appeared), or a lane they use is gone.
- `func bus_choice(seq: Array[int], dest: int) -> Array`: [line id, board tile, alight tile] for a trip along road tiles seq to dest, or [].
- `func line(id: int) -> Line`
- `func count(role: String) -> int`
- `func fleet_size(kind: String) -> int`: Fleet size for CityLife's census (kind as CityLife names it).
- `func spawn_fleet(kind: String, start: Vector2i) -> void`: Adds one vehicle of a fleet (CityLife.external.spawn_fleet).
- `func dispatch_crew(kind: String, station: Vector2i, target: Vector2i, stay: float = 0.0) -> void`: Queues a crew (CityLife.external.dispatch_crew); it leaves when an A* slot is free. A crew called with stay > 0 answers a call, not a sim event: it stays that many seconds at the scene.
- `func step(dt: float) -> void`

## `scripts/fp/traffic/idm.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Intelligent Driver Model (Treiber 2000) in world units (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §3).

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `T = 1.5`: desired time headway, s
- `A = 1.0 * WS.M`: max acceleration, 1 m/s²
- `B = 2.0 * WS.M`: comfortable deceleration, 2 m/s²
- `S0 = 2.0 * WS.M`: jam distance, 2 m
- `DELTA = 4.0`
- `B_MAX = 8.0 * WS.M`: hardest braking the model may ask for

### Functions

- `static func acc(v: float, v0: float, gap: float, dv: float) -> float`: Acceleration for speed v toward desired speed v0 with a leader gap (bumper to bumper) closing at dv = v - v_leader. gap = INF means a free road.
- `static func approach_speed(v_end: float, d: float) -> float`: Speed a car may hold at distance d before a point it must pass at v_end (comfortable braking).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/incidents.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

What a blow in the street means for the city (traffic_feature.gd hit_walker): a resident who was hit remembers it and their mood drops (a shove least, a car or a carjack most, more when knocked down), and residents who saw it remember it too. A punch that knocks someone down, the ASSAULT-th punch within ASSAULT_S or a carjack calls the police; someone a car knocks down, an ambulance (a crew from the nearest station that stays at the scene a while, fleets.gd), each kind at most once per CREW_COOL.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `MOOD = {"shove": -0.5, "punch": -1.0, "car": -2.0, "carjack": -2.0}`
- `DOWN_MOOD = 1.5`
- `SAW_MOOD = -0.3`
- `ASSAULT = 3`
- `ASSAULT_S = 60.0`
- `CREW_COOL = 90.0`
- `STAY = {"police": 40.0, "ambulance": 30.0}`
- `HIT_LINES = { "shove": "got shoved by a visitor %s", "punch": "was punched by a visitor %s", "down"...`: Memory lines (residents.gd remember): what happened to them and what they saw (%s is where).
- `SAW_LINES = { "shove": "saw a visitor shove someone %s", "punch": "saw a visitor punch someone %s",...`

### Functions

- `func setup(p_f: Object) -> void`
- `func report(w: WK.Walker, at: Vector3, strength: float, cause: String, res: Dictionary, seen: Array, by: int = -1) -> Dictionary`: The person_hit info for walker w hit by cause at world point at (res: reactions.gd hit()'s result, seen: the walkers who saw it, by: who struck — -1 the hero, else a walker's id): {"walker", "resident_id", "name", "down", "street", "strength", "by", "witnesses" (their resident ids), "crew" ("police", "ambulance" or "")}. A crew answers the hero's violence only: a blow by someone else never counts toward the assault streak nor dispatches one.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/indicators.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Turn signals: which side a car's indicators blink on, and when a blinking lamp is lit. A car signals the turn of the next junction move (a left or right at a tee or cross, left for a cul-de-sac U-turn) from AHEAD before the move until it has left it; bends in the road are not signalled. A car pulling into a curb slot signals right (toward the curb, right-hand traffic), and one stopped stunned after a knock (shoves.gd) or after running the hero down shows its hazards. render.gd blinks the Light_Indicator_L/R surfaces of the full models.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `VH = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/vehicles.gd")`
- `NONE = 0`
- `LEFT = -1`
- `RIGHT = 1`
- `HAZARD = 2`
- `AHEAD = 30.0 * WS.M`: How far (u) before a junction move a car starts signalling it.
- `RATE = 1.5`: Blinks per second and the lit share of each blink (about 90 a minute, as the rules ask).
- `DUTY = 0.5`

### Functions

- `static func side(c: VH.Car) -> int`: The side c signals now: NONE, LEFT, RIGHT or HAZARD.
- `static func lit(t: float) -> bool`: Whether a blinking lamp is lit at time t (s).
- `static func on(side_: int, s: int, t: float) -> bool`: Whether the left (s < 0) or right lamps of a car signalling side are lit at time t.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/junctions.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Junction control (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §2): 4-way traffic lights on cross tiles (N-S green, amber, all-red, E-W green, ...), priority to the through road on tees, pedestrian walk phases, and the street furniture that shows them: light poles at the four corners, pedestrian signals at both ends of every zebra, and stop or yield signs on tee stems. Lamp states are per-instance material_override swaps from shared on/off materials, never edits of a material.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `LG = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd")`
- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/mesh_kit.gd")`
- `GREEN = 0`
- `AMBER = 1`
- `RED = 2`
- `T_GREEN = 12.0`: Phase lengths, real seconds at 1x (multiplied out by sim.speed through the clock).
- `T_AMBER = 3.0`
- `T_ALLRED = 1.0`
- `CYCLE = 2.0 * (T_GREEN + T_AMBER + T_ALLRED)`
- `WALK_START = 4.5`: People start across a signalled zebra only this early in its walk phase, so they clear the carriageway before the cross traffic gets green.
- `POLE_AT = 0.42`: Corner poles at (±0.42, ±0.42); masts along local -X reach over the inbound lane.
- `MAST = 5.5 * WS.M`
- `PED_SIGNAL_AT = WS.ZEBRA_FAR + 0.3 * WS.M`: Pedestrian signals stand in the curb furniture band just beyond the far edge of their zebra (away from the junction), beside the crossing rather than in its path.
- `CORNERS = [Vector2(1, -1), Vector2(1, 1), Vector2(-1, 1), Vector2(-1, -1)]`: Corners 0..3 = NE, SE, SW, NW: offsets and the approach arm each pole's heads face.
- `CORNER_ARM = [2, 3, 0, 1]`: NE serves northbound traffic (from the S arm), SE eastbound (W arm), SW southbound (N arm), NW westbound (E arm): each on the far side of the junction, mast over the lane.
- `LAMP_COLS = [Color(1.0, 0.12, 0.06), Color(1.0, 0.55, 0.05), Color(0.1, 1.0, 0.45)]`
- `POLE_COL = Color(0.22, 0.23, 0.24)`
- `HOUSING_COL = Color(0.06, 0.065, 0.07)`
- `CONCRETE = Color(0.55, 0.54, 0.52)`
- `SIGN_RED = Color(0.62, 0.04, 0.05)`
- `SIGN_WHITE = Color(0.92, 0.92, 0.9)`

### Properties

- `props: Dictionary`: tile -> {"node": Node3D, "groups": Array[MeshInstance3D] (axis * 3 + colour), "peds": Array[GeometryInstance3D] per (axis * 2 + walk), "poles": Array[Node3D], "state": int, "colliders": Array of holder-local solid entries (written into the view's holder meta)}
- `holder_of: Callable`: The view's tile holder, so our posts can be written into its `colliders` meta (the channel CollisionWorld reads), and the collision refresh to call once they changed. traffic_feature wires both: only its ctx holds the view and the collision world.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_lg: LG, p_root: Node3D) -> void`
- `func offset(i: int) -> float`
- `func phase(i: int) -> Array`: [axis green (0 N-S, 1 E-W), state GREEN/AMBER/RED for that axis, seconds into the state].
- `func light(i: int, e: int) -> int`: Signal for traffic entering cross tile i from arm e (GREEN when the tile has no lights).
- `func green_left(i: int, e: int) -> float`: Seconds of green left for arm e (0 when not green).
- `func ped_walk(i: int, arm: int) -> bool`: True when people may step onto the zebra across arm `arm` of signalled tile i: its walk phase follows the parallel green (zebras across N/S arms walk with E-W green).
- `func ped_lamp(i: int, arm: int) -> bool`: True while the walk lamp of that zebra shows "walk" (the whole parallel green).
- `func rebuild_all() -> void`: (Re)builds the furniture of every junction tile.
- `func build_props(i: int) -> void`: Rebuilds the furniture of tile i (none unless it is a tee or a cross), then writes its solid parts into the tile's colliders.
- `func light_pole(i: int, corner: int) -> Node3D`: The light pole on cross tile i at corner (0..3 = NE, SE, SW, NW), or null.
- `func update_lamps(p: Vector3, r: float) -> void`: Lamp states of cross tiles near p (within r): swaps materials only on change.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/lane_graph.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Right-hand lane graph over the road tiles (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md §1). Pure data: every lane is a polyline sampled every STEP units with cumulative lengths, keyed by (tile, entry edge, exit edge) so a rebuild keeps lane identity (agents hold Lane references). Geometry mirrors RoadTopology and the road GLBs: lane centres LANE_OFFSET right of travel (PASS_OFFSET beside parked cars), corner arcs about the shared tile corner, junction moves from the stop line to the exit edge, a U-turn loop on ends. Also owns the curb parking slots and the blocked-tile set.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `HEAP = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/heap.gd")`
- `STEP = 0.02`
- `DIRS = [Vector2(0, -1), Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(0, 1), Vector2(-1, 0)]`: Arm directions in N, E, S, W order (RoadTopology bit order); y is world +Z.
- `OPP = [2, 3, 0, 1]`
- `STRAIGHT = 0`: Lane kinds.
- `CORNER = 1`
- `APPROACH = 2`
- `MOVE = 3`
- `UTURN = 4`
- `STOP_FRONT = WS.STOP_LINE + WS.STOP_BAR`: Car fronts stop here, measured from the junction centre: on the approach edge of the painted stop line (WS.STOP_LINE, roads.py), which lies just outside the zebra.
- `MOVE_FROM = 0.35`: Where approaches hand over to junction movements. It predates the stop line's move outward and stays put so the movement curves (and their timing) are unchanged; the hold is at STOP_FRONT.
- `ZEBRA_MID = (WS.ZEBRA_NEAR + WS.ZEBRA_FAR) * 0.5`
- `SLOT_ALONG = 3.0 * WS.M`: Curb parking: two slots per side of a straight tile, centres 3 m either side of the middle (6 m spacing); slot k: side k / 2 (0 = right of the run direction), along -/+ for k % 2.
- `SLOTS = 4`
- `SHIFT_LEN = 0.2`: Length of the lateral shift between LANE_OFFSET and PASS_OFFSET at a tile end.
- `SLOT_EDGE_CLEAR = SHIFT_LEN + 0.31 + 0.14`: A slot is unusable when a fixed-offset edge (no compatible straight beyond it) is closer than this along the run: the shift zone plus half the longest moving vehicle (bus) plus half the longest parked one, so no moving AABB ever overlaps a parked AABB.
- `A_LAT = 2.2 * WS.M`: Lateral acceleration used for curve speed limits (2.2 m/s²).
- `UTURN_R = 0.235`: Loop radius of the cul-de-sac U-turn about the turning circle centre.
- `CONFLICT_DIST = 0.11`: Two move lanes whose centrelines come closer than this conflict (a car is 2.1 m wide).
- `BLOCKED_COST = 12.0`: Route cost factor through a blocked tile for the vehicles that may cross one.

### Properties

- `lanes: Array`: id -> Lane or null
- `tiles: Dictionary`: tile -> TileInfo
- `blocked: Dictionary`: tile -> true (broken road, crash or downed line)
- `slots: Dictionary`: Occupied curb slots: (tile * SLOTS + k) -> owner key (String).
- `parked_sides: Dictionary`: Occupied slots per side: (tile * 2 + side) -> count.
- `stop_sides: Dictionary`: Bus-stop sides: tile -> side index whose curb is kept free for the bus.
- `builds: int`: tile rebuilds since setup (tests)
- `bulk: bool`: While true, slot changes skip the lane rebuild (the caller rebuilds once afterwards).
- `dirty: Dictionary`: Tiles whose lanes were rebuilt since the last take_dirty() (agents re-place their nodes).

### Inner classes

- `Lane`: One lane: a directed polyline on one road tile.
- `TileInfo`: Per road tile: its mask, piece and lanes.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim) -> void`
- `func clear() -> void`
- `func rebuild_all() -> void`: Rebuilds every road tile in sim.active.
- `func rebuild_around(i: int) -> void`: Rebuilds tile i and its four neighbours (a road tile was built or cleared).
- `func neighbours(i: int) -> Array[int]`: In-bounds 4-neighbour tile indices of i.
- `func is_empty() -> bool`
- `func lane_count() -> int`
- `func info(i: int) -> TileInfo`
- `func across(i: int, e: int) -> int`: Tile across edge e of tile i, or -1.
- `func entry(i: int, e: int) -> Array`: Lanes that begin at edge e of tile i (a junction's approach, else the through lane).
- `func next_lanes(l: Lane) -> Array`: Lanes an agent can take after reaching the end of l.
- `func prev_lanes(l: Lane) -> Array`: Lanes that end where l begins (upstream), for gap checks.
- `func lane_between(i: int, fe: int, te: int) -> Lane`: The lane on tile i from entry edge fe to exit edge te (a move for junctions), or null.
- `func pos_at(l: Lane, s: float) -> Vector2`: World xz of the point at distance s along l (clamped to the lane).
- `func tan_at(l: Lane, s: float) -> Vector2`: Unit tangent of l at distance s.
- `func project(l: Lane, p: Vector2) -> float`: Distance along l of the point closest to p (xz).
- `func pass_factor(l: Lane, s: float) -> float`: How far a straight lane is pulled in toward PASS_OFFSET at s (0 = LANE_OFFSET, 1 = PASS_OFFSET).
- `func refresh_blocked() -> bool`: Re-reads broken roads and road-blocking events (car_crash, power_line). Returns true on change.
- `func is_blocked(i: int) -> bool`
- `func parkable(i: int) -> bool`: True when straight tile i can take curb parking at all (paved: not a bridge, a junction or a track without curbs).
- `func run_dir(i: int) -> Vector2`: Run direction (xz) of straight tile i.
- `func side_of_heading(i: int, h: Vector2) -> int`: Side index (0 right of run_dir, 1 left) of straight tile i that a vehicle heading h drives on.
- `func slot_pose(i: int, k: int) -> Array`: [pos: Vector2 (world xz), heading: Vector2] of curb slot k of straight tile i. The car faces the traffic on its side (right-hand).
- `func slot_valid(i: int, k: int) -> bool`: True when slot k of tile i is usable: a parkable straight, clear of fixed-offset edges (where the moving lane cannot shift outside the tile) and of a bus-stop curb.
- `func slot_free(i: int, k: int) -> bool`
- `func slot_owner(i: int, k: int) -> String`
- `func set_slot(i: int, k: int, owner: String) -> void`: Marks curb slot k of tile i as taken by owner (or freed with ""), rebuilding the lanes beside it when its side changes between empty and occupied.
- `func side_parked(i: int, sidx: int) -> bool`
- `func slots_on_heading(i: int, h: Vector2) -> Array[int]`: Slot indices on the curb a vehicle heading h on straight tile i would pull into.
- `func rebuild_tile(i: int) -> void`: Rebuilds the lanes of tile i from sim.kind and RoadTopology (removes them when it is no road).
- `func take_dirty() -> Dictionary`: Tiles rebuilt since the last call (and clears the set).
- `static func entry_pt(e: int, off: float) -> Vector2`: Tile-local entry point on edge e for traffic heading into the tile at lateral offset off.
- `static func exit_pt(e: int, off: float) -> Vector2`: Tile-local exit point on edge e for traffic leaving the tile at lateral offset off.
- `func lanes_along(seq: Array[int], fe0: int = -1, te_last: int = -1) -> Array`: Lane path along a sequence of road tiles: for each tile the lane from the edge it is entered by to the edge toward the next tile, with junction approaches before their moves. fe0 is the entry edge of the first tile (-1: any), te_last the exit edge of the last (-1: any). O(tiles). Returns [] when a step has no lane.
- `func edge_between(a: int, b: int) -> int`: Edge of tile a that faces adjacent tile b, or -1.
- `func lanes_through(i: int, fe: int, te: int) -> Array`: Lanes crossing tile i entering at fe and leaving at te (either may be -1 for "any").
- `func astar(from: Lane, goals: Dictionary, max_nodes: int = 3000, through_blocked: bool = false) -> Array`: A* over lanes from the end of `from` to the end of any lane in `goals` (lane id -> true), costing length / limit * (1 + 2 * traffic) and avoiding blocked tiles (through_blocked: crews and bus lines may cross them, at BLOCKED_COST times the cost, when there is no way round). At most max_nodes expansions. Returns the lanes after `from` up to and including the goal lane, or [].

extends `RefCounted`

Builds merged, vertex-coloured meshes for E's procedural stand-ins (traffic lights, signs, the far LOD of every vehicle and person model). One surface per mesh, so a whole junction's poles or a whole car costs one draw.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`

- `func box(xf: Transform3D, sz: Vector3, c: Color) -> void`: Axis-aligned box of size sz (units) centred at the origin of xf, coloured c.
- `func cyl(xf: Transform3D, r0: float, r1: float, h: float, c: Color, sides: int = 10, caps: bool = true) -> void`: Cylinder along +Y from the origin of xf: radius r0 at the bottom, r1 at the top, height h.
- `func disc(xf: Transform3D, r: float, c: Color, sides: int = 12, rot: float = 0.0) -> void`: Flat regular polygon (disc with `sides` corners) of radius r in the xf's XY plane, facing +Z.

- `func mesh(xf: Transform3D, m: Mesh, overrides: Array = []) -> void`: Appends every surface of a mesh, coloured by its material albedo (emission adds a glow tint).
- `func node(root: Node3D) -> void`: Merges every MeshInstance3D under root (in root space) into one vertex-coloured mesh.
- `func commit() -> ArrayMesh`: The merged mesh (null when nothing was added).
- `static func vc_material(rough: float = 0.6, metal: float = 0.0) -> StandardMaterial3D`: Shared opaque material for vertex-coloured meshes.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/occupants.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Drivers seated in the moving vehicles nearest the camera. Only while a vehicle draws its full model: those have see-through glass, a cabin and a Seat_Driver marker at the driver's hip point (tools/blender/realcity/vehicles2.py); the merged far LODs have opaque glass. A driver is the car's resident (people.dress picks the same avatar and stature the resident walks with) or an ambient body from the city seed, posed once in the sit loop with its mixers off, so a seated body costs its draws and nothing per frame beyond its transform. A bicycle's rider pedals instead (the ride loop, casting a shadow), on every bicycle drawn in full (a bicycle's far LOD carries a rough rider of its own).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/people.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Animated people from HC's roster (docs/fp/slices/E-traffic.md deliverable 9, TPS_PLAN §1.10-1.11). Rocketbox bodies on Godot's humanoid skeleton, picked by job, gender and crc32(resident id) for residents and by HC's ambient weights for the crowd, each under a CharacterRoot scaled to a jittered stature, animated by the gender's shared library plus three clips layered here at load (walk_carry and carry_idle hold a box, walk_phone a phone at the ear), with the playback rate matched to the walking speed so feet do not slide. LOD tiers by camera distance, 10 % hysteresis: T0  <= 12 m, max 8   AnimationTree (state machine, 0.25 s crossfades), every frame, shadows T1  12-30 m           AnimationPlayer advanced by hand, 30 Hz to 20 m (shadows) else 15 Hz T2  30-60 m           the same at 10 Hz, no shadows T3  to VIS_PERSON     HC's static mid-stride <Name>_lod1 in one MultiMesh per avatar T1 and T2 share a cap of SKIN_CAP bodies on screen, and everything stays inside DRAW_CAP character draws. Off-screen bodies keep their pose with their mixer inactive (and go back to the pool after OFF_KEEP). Bodies are pooled per avatar and instanced at most NEW_PER_FRAME per frame. Body and lod1 scenes load on background threads when first needed (a first load takes 25-150 ms; loading every avatar up front costs ~100 MB of textures); a walker whose body is still loading waits at T3, undrawn while its lod1 loads too. Asset building lives in people_kit.gd; the body pool and the scene cache live in people_pool.gd (this class keeps the public API and delegates).

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/people_kit.gd")`
- `POOL = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/people_pool.gd")`
- `WebSupport = preload("res://scripts/ops/web_support.gd")`
- `T0_R = 12.0 * WS.M`
- `T0_CAP = 8`
- `T1_R = 30.0 * WS.M`
- `T1_NEAR = 20.0 * WS.M`
- `T2_R = 60.0 * WS.M`
- `HYST = 1.1`
- `SKIN_CAP = 40`
- `DRAW_CAP = 150`
- `HZ_NEAR = 30.0`
- `HZ_MID = 15.0`
- `HZ_FAR = 10.0`
- `NEW_PER_FRAME = 4`
- `OFF_KEEP = 4.0`
- `LOOK_CAP = 6`
- `XFADE = 0.25`
- `WALK_ON = 0.35 * WS.M`: A person counts as walking above WALK_ON and as standing below WALK_OFF (u/s, as drawn).
- `WALK_OFF = 0.2 * WS.M`
- `RATE_MIN = 0.5`
- `RATE_MAX = 1.6`
- `PERSON_FADE = 0.4`: People fade out over this last stretch before VIS_PERSON (T3).
- `CULL_UP = 0.9 * WS.M`: Frustum test: a sphere around the body (metres above the feet, radius).
- `CULL_R = 1.3 * WS.M`
- `STATES = KIT.STATES`
- `LOCO = [&"walk", &"walk_carry", &"walk_phone"]`
- `STILL = [&"", &"carry_idle", &"phone"]`
- `BOX_COLOR = Color(0.62, 0.47, 0.3)`

### Properties

- `ok: bool`: The instanced-body class lives in people_pool.gd (the pool owns the bodies' lifecycle).

### Inner classes

- `Avatar`: One roster body (never a hero).

### Functions

- `func load_assets() -> bool`: Loads the roster and both libraries and builds the layered clips and the T0 tree. False (with `why`) when HC's characters are missing: E then draws the legacy static people.
- `func reset(p_root: Node3D, city_seed: int) -> void`: Starts drawing under p_root (a new world): frees every body, keeps the loaded assets.
- `func clear() -> void`: Frees every body and LOD layer.
- `func crc32(s: String) -> int`: CRC-32 (IEEE, as zlib) of s's UTF-8 bytes.
- `func resident_gender(rid: String, full_name: String) -> String`: Gender of a resident: HC's name_gender for the first name, else crc32(id) & 1 (1 = f).
- `func resident_avatar(rid: String, full_name: String, job: String) -> int`: Avatar index for a resident: the job's pool for the gender, else the gender's casual pool, indexed by crc32(id). -1 when nothing fits.
- `func stature(g: String, u: float) -> float`: Stature (m) for a gender and a 0..1 jitter value.
- `func dress(w: WK.Walker, residents: Variant) -> void`: Gives w its avatar and stature (once): residents by their id, ambient walkers from the city seed.
- `func avatar_name(w: WK.Walker) -> String`: Avatar name of walker w ("" before it is dressed).
- `func scale_of(w: WK.Walker) -> float`: CharacterRoot scale of w: WS.M * h_target / rest_height_m.
- `func authored_speed(w: WK.Walker, clip: StringName) -> float`: Ground speed (u/s) clip covers at playback rate 1 on w's body.
- `func head_of(w: WK.Walker, base: Vector3) -> Vector3`: World position of w's Head bone while a body draws it, else an estimate from its stature.
- `func begin(delta: float, adt: float, cam: Camera3D, cam_pos: Vector3, look_at: Vector3) -> void`: Starts a frame: delta is real seconds, adt game seconds (delta * sim.speed).
- `func on_screen(p: Vector3) -> bool`: True when a body at feet position p could be on screen.
- `func add(w: WK.Walker, d: float, residents: Variant) -> void`: Queues walker w (eased already, d = camera distance) and advances its clip.
- `func finish() -> void`: Assigns tiers, attaches, advances and releases bodies, and fills the T3 layers.
- `func seat(w: WK.Walker) -> bool`: Gives dressed walker w a body outside the tiers (a seated driver, posed by occupants.gd); false while none is free. release(w) hands it back. The pool (people_pool.gd) does the work.
- `func release(w: WK.Walker) -> void`: A walker leaves for good (removed): its body goes back to the pool.
- `func finish_loads() -> void`
- `func stats() -> Dictionary`: anim_stats() for G2's bench: tier counts on screen, microseconds advancing mixers this frame, character draws (skinned surfaces and boxes on screen plus two per T3 avatar layer).

## `scripts/fp/traffic/people_kit.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Asset building for people.gd: the layered clips (a box held in both hands, a phone at the ear), the shared T0 AnimationTree, and HC's lod1 meshes as dither-fading T3 MultiMesh layers; the clips reactions.gd plays (blows, falls, running off) and how their time runs.

### Constants

- `ARM_PARTS = [ "Shoulder", "UpperArm", "LowerArm", "Hand", "ThumbMetacarpal", "ThumbProximal", "Thum...`: Layered clips: the arm bones taken from another clip's pose at a fixed time.
- `CARRY_AT = 0.0`
- `PHONE_AT = 0.5`
- `NEEDS = [ &"idle", &"walk", &"talk", &"talk_2", &"phone", &"carry", &"idle_look", &"idle_wait",...`
- `STATES = [ &"idle", &"idle_look", &"idle_wait", &"walk", &"walk_carry", &"walk_phone", &"carry_i...`: Every clip the T0 tree holds: HC's walking and standing clips, the layered ones, and the reactions (reactions.gd), the punches of someone fighting back among them.
- `ONE_SHOTS = [ &"knockback", &"get_up", &"hit_head", &"hit_chest", &"wave", &"yes", &"punch_jab", &"...`: Reactions that play once and hold their last frame (the rest loop), the blows among them, and the quicker crossfade into a blow (s): it lands at once.
- `BLOWS = [&"knockback", &"hit_head", &"hit_chest"]`
- `REACT_XFADE = 0.08`
- `T3_SHADER = """`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `WebSupport = preload("res://scripts/ops/web_support.gd")`

### Functions

- `static func layered_library(hc: AnimationLibrary) -> Variant`: A copy of HC's library with walk_carry, carry_idle and walk_phone added; the name of the first missing clip in NEEDS instead when it lacks one.
- `static func layer(base: Animation, over: Animation, bones: Array[String], at: float, nm: String) -> Animation`: base with the rotations of `bones` replaced by over's pose at time `at` (constant keys).
- `static func build_tree(states: Array[StringName], xfade: float) -> AnimationNodeBlendTree`: The T0 tree, shared by every body: state machine (every state reaches every other with a crossfade, REACT_XFADE into a blow) -> TimeSeek (handovers from T1) -> TimeScale (playback rate) -> output.
- `static func clip_time(clip: StringName, t: float, ln: float) -> float`: Time t into a clip of length ln: one-shots stop on their last frame, loops wrap.
- `static func t3_shader() -> Shader`
- `static func lod_mesh(ps: PackedScene, shader: Shader) -> Array`: The first mesh of a lod1 scene as [ArrayMesh with the fade shader, its transform in the scene]; [] when the scene has no mesh.
- `static func t3_layer(nm: String, mesh: Mesh) -> MultiMeshInstance3D`: An empty, hidden T3 layer for mesh (custom data carries the fade).
- `static func fill(mmi: MultiMeshInstance3D, xfs: Array[Transform3D], cols: Array[Color]) -> void`: Shows xfs (fade in the alpha of cols) on mmi, growing its buffer by doubling.
- `static func crc32(s: String) -> int`: CRC-32 (IEEE, as zlib) of s's UTF-8 bytes.
- `static func pose(sk: Skeleton3D, bone: int) -> Transform3D`: Bone pose in skeleton space from the local poses.
- `static func scene(pe: RefCounted, path: String) -> PackedScene`: The PackedScene at path: loaded at once when pe.blocking, else from a background load (null while that runs, and for good when it fails or the file is missing).
- `static func finish_loads(pe: RefCounted) -> void`: Waits for every background scene load still running and keeps the results.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/people_pool.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The body pool and scene cache behind people.gd (split out so people.gd stays under the 1000-line cap; the public API stays on people, which delegates here). Owns the PackedScene cache (_scenes / _pending / scene_loads; the load mechanics are people_kit.gd's statics with this pool as their `pe`), the free Body instances per avatar, the bodies lent by seat(), and the take / attach / detach / release lifecycle. people.gd keeps the roster, the avatar pick (dress), and the per-frame tier pipeline; it reaches this pool through `_pool`, and this pool reaches back (avatars, _active, root, the roster-built libraries and box transforms, the _set_mode animation helper) through a WEAKREF so the pair does not leak at exit_fp.

### Constants

- `KIT = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/people_kit.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `NEW_PER_FRAME = 4`: Bodies are instanced at most this many per frame (the rest wait for a pooled one).

### Properties

- `blocking: bool`: Load body and lod1 scenes on the calling thread (deterministic tests), not in the background.
- `scene_loads: int`: Body-scene load initiations; tests assert a dressed walker's seat/take adds none.

### Inner classes

- `Body`: One instanced body: CharacterRoot > the body scene (Armature/GeneralSkeleton/Body, Anim, Tree).

### Functions

- `func begin_frame() -> void`: New frame: the per-frame instancing budget resets (people.begin).
- `func scene(path: String) -> PackedScene`: The PackedScene at path: loaded at once when blocking, else from a background load (null while that runs, and for good when it fails or the file is missing). A dumb loader: the callers own the policy (dress warms at pick time on threaded builds, reset pre-warms on no-threads ones). Mechanics in people_kit.
- `func is_pending(path: String) -> bool`: True while a background load of path is still running (a finished or failed one reads false).
- `func finish_loads() -> void`: Waits for every background scene load still running and keeps the results.
- `func prewarm_ambient(groups: Array, avatars: Array) -> void`: Loads every ambient avatar's body scene up front: on no-threads builds (the web export) this blocks at world build so play never hitches on a first seat or take; on threaded builds tests call it directly (in-game, dress-time requests warm the same paths lazily). One scene at a time: the headless dummy renderer's RID/material storage races when many threaded loads finalize together, and a loading screen does not need the parallelism.
- `func take(ai: int) -> Body`: A pooled body of avatar ai, or a new one within this frame's budget once its scene has loaded.
- `func seat(w: WK.Walker) -> bool`: Seats walker w on a body lent out of the pool (drivers, riders): the body stays out of the per-frame pipeline until release. False when none is available yet.
- `func attach(w: WK.Walker, tier: int, frame: int) -> bool`: Gives w a body (pooled, or new within this frame's budget), stamped with the people's frame. False when none is available.
- `func detach(w: WK.Walker) -> void`: Returns w's body (if any) to its pool.
- `func release_body(b: Body) -> void`
- `func release(w: WK.Walker) -> void`: A walker leaves for good (removed): its body goes back to the pool.
- `func clear() -> void`: Frees the pooled and the lent bodies (people.clear frees the active ones and the rest).
- `func make(ai: int) -> Body`
- `func ensure_box(b: Body, g: String) -> void`: A cardboard box held in front of the chest (carry poses), parented to UpperChest.

## `scripts/fp/traffic/reactions.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

People hit in the street (docs/fp/ARCHITECTURE.md, Body actions): shoved or punched by the player, struck by the car they drive or dragged out of their own (carjack). A light blow makes the person reel (hit_chest, hit_head) and slide back a little; a hard one (DOWN), the HITS_DOWN-th punch in a row or a fast car knocks them down (knockback), and they lie a while before they get up (get_up). A car that runs them over where they lie shoves them along and leaves them down but up sooner. Then they shake their head or shout at whoever did it, run off, or walk back to where they were; some of those shoved or punched fight back instead (fight_back): they square up to the hero, close in and throw jabs and crosses (on_hero_hit) until the hero is down, gets away or drives off — each their own way (fight_tempers), fixed to who they are: one turns the hero's blows aside, one sidesteps round them while they wait, one calls friends over, one squares up and bolts, and a tough one leads with the cross and answers a blow at once. People within WITNESS_R who see it run off or shout too. While a walker stands where the blow left it its state is "react" (it keeps its edge and plan; the slide and the walk back move only its drawn offset), and a run gives it its own state back at RUN_F times its pace with the run clip. The hero may take hold of someone (grab): they hang in the hero's hands (hold_to) in HOLD_CLIP, reeling from blows without falling free, until let go (release), knocked down or HOLD_S is up, then react as to a shove. A punch thrown at the hero is announced as it starts (on_wind_up), holds back then snaps through its wind-up (counter_cues) and may be countered as it arrives (on_hero_parry). What follows a blow for the city (memory, mood, crews) is incidents.gd's.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `AP = preload("res://scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd")`
- `WK = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/walkers.gd")`
- `BS = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/body_spheres.gd")`
- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `FB = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/fight_back.gd")`: The scrap and the care for a body on the ground, split out of this file: fighting back, the tempers, counter cues and downed awareness live there. This file keeps the Reaction records and the after-blow plans; the layer borrows them (its back-link is a weakref). The aliases further down keep the old RE.* names working for tests and benches.
- `CR = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/crowd_reacts.gd")`: The crowd's answer to what the street sees and hears (the knock-down gasp, the horn startle), split out the same way; its constants stay under the old names via the alias below.
- `TI = preload("res://scripts/fp/traffic/throw_impact.gd")`
- `LENGTHS = {&"knockback": 0.833, &"get_up": 1.54, &"hit_head": 0.417, &"hit_chest": 0.333}`: Clip lengths (s) in HC's libraries (the female clips match); setup() reads them again.
- `ONCE = [&"knockback", &"get_up", &"hit_head", &"hit_chest"]`: Clips that play once: the walker does not turn while they run (it may be lying down).
- `WITNESS_R = 8.0 * WS.M`
- `DOWN = 0.7`: A blow this strong (0..1) knocks a person down, and so does the HITS_DOWN-th punch within HITS_S seconds.
- `HITS_DOWN = 3`
- `HITS_S = 8.0`
- `RUN_F = 2.6`
- `BACK_V = 1.1 * WS.M`
- `BODY_R = 0.25 * WS.M`
- `BODY_H = 1.7 * WS.M`
- `HEAD_R = 0.14 * WS.M`
- `DOWN_REACH = 0.4 * WS.M`: A fall sweeps the posed body this far past the drawn feet (the clip's tip, the lie's reach), so a knock-down's slide clamps them that much clear besides its capsule: the fall needs its own floor, and landing against the wall leaves the lie and the rise inside it.
- `SEE = [0.3, 0.6, 0.85]`: Share of the people around who react, and of those the share who run off, by severity (a shove, a punch, a knock-down).
- `FLEE = [0.15, 0.5, 0.6]`
- `ANSWERS = { "wave": [10.0, 0.75, 0.0, &"wave", 2.8], "yes": [5.0, 0.75, 0.0, &"yes", 2.5], "no": ...`: Who answers an emote of the hero's: [range (m), the cosine of the cone ahead, share, clip, seconds]. A share of 0 is the nearest person in the cone; otherwise each of those around answers with that chance, at most ANSWER_MAX of them.
- `ANSWER_MAX = 4`
- `FIGHT_ODDS = FB.FIGHT_ODDS`: The fight layer's constants under their old names, for the tests and benches that read them; fight_back.gd (FB) owns them now.
- `FIGHT_BLOWS = FB.FIGHT_BLOWS`
- `FIGHT_REACH = FB.FIGHT_REACH`
- `WIND_RATE = FB.WIND_RATE`
- `CHECK_NEAR = FB.CHECK_NEAR`
